en: expose; reveal publicly (a secret or wrongdoing)

examples.en: A reporter exposed the company's secret.

examples.ko: 그 직원은 회사의 문제를 뉴스에서 폭로할 거예요.
examples.en: That employee will reveal the company's problems on the news.

examples.ko: 경찰이 범인의 거짓말을 폭로하는 증거를 찾았어요.
examples.en: The police found evidence that exposes the criminal's lie.

examples.ko: 누가 우리 가게 이야기를 인터넷에 폭로해서 화가 났어요.
examples.en: Someone exposed our shop's story online, so I got angry.
After revealing the secret, I felt relieved.

examples.ko: 회사의 돈 문제를 폭로한 기사가 화제예요.
examples.en: The article that exposed the company's money problems is the talk of the town.

explain: 숨겨진 나쁜 일이나 비밀을 세상에 알릴 때 써요. 뉴스와 기사에서 자주 들리고, 일상 대화에서는 '털어놓다'가 더 부드러워요. '비밀을 폭로하다', '문제를 폭로하다'처럼 같이 써요.
explain_en: Use it when you make a hidden wrongdoing or secret known to the public. It shows up in news and articles; in everyday talk '털어놓다' (to confess) is softer. It pairs with words like '비밀을 폭로하다' and '문제를 폭로하다'.

examples.en: Our team established a new rule.

examples.ko: 어릴 때부터 좋은 생활 습관을 확립하면 좋아요.
examples.en: It's good to build healthy habits from childhood.
The company works to establish a safe workplace.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 자기만의 스타일을 확립해서 유명해졌어요.
examples.en: That singer established a style of their own and became famous.

examples.ko: 학교에서 서로 존중하는 문화를 확립할 거예요.
examples.en: We will establish a culture of mutual respect at school.

examples.ko: 한번 확립한 원칙은 쉽게 바꾸지 않아요.
examples.en: Once a principle is firmly set, we don't change it easily.

explain: 습관, 제도, 질서, 원칙처럼 눈에 보이지 않는 것에 써요. '세우다'보다 흔들리지 않게 단단히 만든다는 느낌이 강해요. '확립되다'는 그렇게 자리 잡은 결과를 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: It goes with things you can't see, such as habits, systems, order, and principles. Compared with '세우다' (to set up), it suggests making something firm so it won't waver. '확립되다' describes the result, when something has become settled.

en: take part (in a cause); join in

examples.en: I'll join this environmental campaign too.
Many citizens took part in the event.

examples.ko: 친구들이 다 동참하니까 저도 하고 싶어요.
examples.en: All my friends are joining, so I want to do it too.

examples.ko: 우리 반 모두 기부에 동참해 주세요.
examples.en: Everyone in our class, please join the donation drive.

examples.ko: 동참하고 싶은 사람은 손을 들어 주세요.
examples.en: Anyone who wants to join, please raise your hand.

examples.ko: 이 일에 동참한 분들께 정말 감사해요.
examples.en: I'm truly grateful to everyone who joined in this effort.

explain: '참가하다'는 대회나 모임에 들어가는 것이고, '동참하다'는 어떤 뜻이나 운동에 같은 마음으로 함께한다는 느낌이에요. 기부, 캠페인, 운동과 잘 어울리고 '~에 동참하다'로 써요.
explain_en: '참가하다' is entering a contest or gathering, while '동참하다' means joining a cause or movement with the same spirit. It suits donations, campaigns, and drives, and takes '~에' (e.g., '캠페인에 동참하다').

examples.en: I will surely repay your kindness.
I want to repay my parents' love.

examples.ko: 저는 선생님의 기대에 보답하려고 열심히 공부해요.
examples.en: I study hard to live up to my teacher's expectations.
How should I repay their kindness?

examples.ko: 그 선수는 팬들의 응원에 우승으로 보답했어요.
examples.en: The player repaid the fans' support with a championship.
I bought dinner as a way of saying thanks.

explain: 받은 도움이나 기대에 행동으로 돌려줄 때 써요. '갚다'는 빌린 돈에도 쓰지만 '보답하다'는 감사의 마음이 담긴 점잖은 말이에요. '은혜에', '기대에', '응원에'처럼 '~에'와 함께 써요.
explain_en: Use it when you give back, through action, for help or expectations you received. '갚다' also covers borrowed money, but '보답하다' is a more dignified word full of gratitude. It takes '~에', as in '은혜에', '기대에', '응원에'.

examples.en: I put a poster up on the wall.
Please post the notice on the door.
Some schools have you attach a name tag to your bag.
I stuck a label on the box and then sent it.
The spot you attach it to must be clean for it to last.
Attach the receipt to the form and then submit it.

explain: '붙이다'와 같은 뜻이지만 '부착하다'는 안내문, 스티커, 장치처럼 격식 있는 글이나 설명서에서 써요. 일상 대화에서는 거의 '붙이다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It means the same as '붙이다' but appears in formal writing such as notices, stickers, devices, and manuals. In everyday talk people almost always say '붙이다'.

examples.en: I'm truly sorry the result turned out this way.
Unfortunately, I can't make it to this gathering.
I have some unfortunate news to share.
Unfortunately, the tickets are all sold out.

examples.ko: 그 일이 일어난 것이 아주 유감스러웠어요.
examples.en: It was very regrettable that it happened.
He said it was regrettable that the promise wasn't kept.

explain: 서운하고 아쉬운 마음을 공손하게 말할 때 써요. '아쉽다'보다 격식 있어서 거절이나 안 좋은 소식을 전할 때 자주 나와요. '유감이다'도 같은 뜻으로 많이 쓰고, 친구와는 '아쉽다'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It politely expresses disappointment or regret. It is more formal than '아쉽다', so it often appears when declining or delivering bad news. '유감이다' is used just as often, and with friends '아쉽다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: The government decided to crack down on illegal ads.
The school took disciplinary action against a student who broke the rules.

examples.ko: 여러 나라가 그 나라를 제재한 뒤 무역이 줄었어요.
examples.en: After several countries imposed sanctions, trade decreased.
Extreme behavior has to be restricted.

examples.ko: 나쁜 말을 쓴 사용자를 제재하는 규칙이 생겼어요.
examples.en: A rule was made to penalize users who use abusive language.

examples.ko: 협회가 선수를 제재하면 경기에 나갈 수 없어요.
examples.en: If the association sanctions a player, they can't play in games.

explain: 규칙이나 법을 어긴 사람, 회사, 나라에게 불이익을 주어 활동을 막거나 제한할 때 써요. '벌하다'는 벌 자체에 초점이 있어요. 뉴스에서는 '경제 제재'로 자주 들려요.
explain_en: Use it when you penalize a person, company, or country that broke rules or laws by limiting or blocking their activity. '벌하다' focuses on punishment itself. In the news you often hear it in '경제 제재' (economic sanctions).

examples.en: The construction team demolished the old building with explosives.
In the movie, the hero blows up a bridge.
They will blast the rock to make a tunnel.
Everyone was evacuated before the blast.

examples.ko: 폭탄으로 건물을 폭파한 범인을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: They are searching for the criminal who blew up the building.

examples.ko: 낡은 굴뚝을 폭파하면 큰 소리가 나요.
examples.en: Blowing up an old chimney makes a loud noise.

explain: 폭탄이나 화약으로 건물, 다리, 바위처럼 큰 것을 터뜨려 부술 때 써요. '터뜨리다'는 풍선, 웃음, 울음에도 쓰지만 '폭파하다'는 큰 구조물에만 써요. 뉴스와 영화 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Use it when blasting big things such as buildings, bridges, or rock with bombs or explosives. '터뜨리다' also works for balloons, laughter, and tears, but '폭파하다' is only for large structures. It is common in news and movie talk.

examples.ko: 회사가 이번 사고에 사과의 뜻을 표명했어요.
examples.en: The company expressed its apology for this accident.
The parents sent a letter expressing their concern.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 내년에 은퇴하겠다는 뜻을 표명할 거예요.
examples.en: That player will announce the intention to retire next year.
You have to state your opinion clearly to avoid misunderstanding.

examples.ko: 감사의 마음을 표명하고 싶어서 편지를 썼어요.
examples.en: I wanted to express my gratitude, so I wrote a letter.

examples.ko: 다들 반대한다고 표명한 뒤에 회의가 끝났어요.
examples.en: The meeting ended after everyone stated their opposition.

explain: 생각, 입장, 뜻을 공식적으로 분명하게 밝힐 때 써요. '말하다'보다 훨씬 딱딱해서 뉴스, 발표문, 공식 편지에 나와요. '의사를 표명하다', '입장을 표명하다', '유감을 표명하다'처럼 같이 써요.
explain_en: Use it when you officially and clearly state a thought, position, or intention. It is much stiffer than '말하다' and appears in news, announcements, and formal letters. It pairs as '의사를 표명하다', '입장을 표명하다', '유감을 표명하다'.

examples.ko: 남자와 여자는 동등한 기회를 가져야 해요.
examples.en: Men and women should have equal opportunities.
The two teams are almost equal in skill.
Everyone is equal before the law.
We talked on equal footing.

examples.ko: 이 자격증은 대학 졸업과 동등하게 인정돼요.
examples.en: This certificate is recognized as equal to a university degree.

examples.ko: 두 사람이 동등하지 않다고 느껴져서 속상했어요.
examples.en: I felt upset because the two people didn't seem to be on equal terms.

explain: '같다'는 모양이나 수가 똑같을 때도 쓰지만 '동등하다'는 자격, 권리, 위치, 수준이 같을 때 써요. '동등한 대우', '동등한 관계'처럼 명사 앞에 올 때가 많아요. '평등하다'는 차별이 없다는 뜻에 더 가까워요.
explain_en: '같다' can describe identical shape or number, but '동등하다' is for equal qualification, rights, position, or level. It often comes before a noun, as in '동등한 대우' or '동등한 관계'. '평등하다' is closer to 'free of discrimination'.

examples.en: Regular exercise improves your health.

examples.ko: 두 나라는 우호를 증진하기 위해 만났어요.
examples.en: The two countries met to promote friendship.

examples.ko: 비타민은 면역력을 증진하는 데 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: Vitamins help boost immunity.

examples.ko: 이 프로그램은 아이들의 학습 능력을 증진해 줘요.
examples.en: This program improves children's learning ability.
There is research saying walking improves stamina.

examples.ko: 건강을 증진하고 싶으면 잠을 충분히 자요.
examples.en: If you want to improve your health, get enough sleep.

explain: 건강, 체력, 복지, 친선처럼 좋은 것을 더 좋아지게 할 때 써요. '늘리다'는 수나 양에 두루 쓰지만 '증진하다'는 건강·능력·관계 같은 말과 주로 어울려요. 뉴스와 안내문에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: Use it when you make something good even better, such as health, stamina, welfare, or friendly relations. '늘리다' works for any number or amount, while '증진하다' mostly goes with health, ability, and relationships. You see it often in news and notices.

en: the whole world; under heaven (all there is)

examples.ko: 천하에 둘도 없는 친구라서 늘 고마워요.
examples.en: He's a friend like no other in the world, so I'm always grateful.

examples.ko: 그는 천하를 다 가진 것처럼 기뻐했어요.
examples.en: He was delighted as if he owned the whole world.
They say a powerful general ruled the realm long ago.

examples.ko: 시험이 끝나니까 천하가 내 것 같아요.
examples.en: Now that exams are over, the world feels like mine.
Even the laziest person under the sun got up early today.
This singer's skill is recognized by the whole world.

explain: 원래는 '하늘 아래 온 세상'이라는 옛말이에요. 지금은 '천하의 + 사람'으로 강조하거나 '천하를 얻은 기분'처럼 과장해서 말할 때 써요. '세상'보다 옛이야기나 과장하는 말투에 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: be carefree; not worry at all
phrases.nuance_ko: 걱정할 일이 있는데도 아무 걱정 없이 느긋한 사람을 말해요. 약간 놀리거나 어이없는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes someone relaxed with no worries even when there is something to worry about. It carries a slightly teasing or exasperated tone.

explain_en: Originally an old word for everything under heaven. Today it appears in the emphasizing pattern '천하의 + person' or in exaggeration like '천하를 얻은 기분'. It fits old stories and exaggerated speech better than the plain '세상'.

examples.en: I formed a band with my friends.
The students are trying to form a club.
The neighbors will form a residents' group.

examples.ko: 모임을 결성한 지 벌써 일 년이에요.
examples.en: It's already been a year since we formed the group.
Before forming it, we decided on a name first.
We'll form a team and enter the contest.

explain: 사람들이 모여 밴드, 동아리, 조합 같은 단체를 공식적으로 만들 때 써요. '만들다'보다 딱딱하고, '모이다'와 달리 조직을 이룬다는 느낌이에요. 보통 '팀, 모임, 밴드, 연합'과 같이 써요.
explain_en: Use it when people officially set up a group such as a band, club, or union. It is stiffer than '만들다' and, unlike '모이다', suggests an organization is formed. It typically pairs with '팀', '모임', '밴드', '연합'.

examples.ko: 이웃과 대화를 끊으면 자신을 고립시키게 돼요.
examples.en: If you stop talking to neighbors, you end up isolating yourself.
Heavy snow cut off the village.

examples.ko: 친구들이 그 아이를 고립시키면 안 돼요.
examples.en: Friends must not isolate that child.

examples.ko: 홍수가 섬을 고립시켜서 배가 못 갔어요.
examples.en: The flood cut off the island, so boats couldn't go.

examples.ko: 새로 온 직원을 일부러 고립시켜도 문제는 해결되지 않아요.
examples.en: Deliberately isolating the new employee will not solve the problem.

examples.ko: 일부러 사람을 고립시키는 것은 나쁜 행동이에요.
examples.en: Deliberately isolating a person is bad behavior.

explain: '고립되다'는 어떤 사람이나 곳이 혼자가 된 상태이고, '고립시키다'는 누군가를 떨어지게 만드는 행동이라는 점이 달라요. 사람에게 쓰면 따돌림처럼 나쁜 느낌이 있고, 눈이나 홍수 같은 자연 현상과도 써요.
explain_en: '고립되다' is the state of being left alone, while '고립시키다' is the act of making someone or somewhere cut off. With people it carries a bad, bullying-like feeling, and it also works with natural events such as snow or floods.

en: feel sorry for; pity; sympathize with

examples.en: I felt sorry for the child crying on the street.
Everyone feels sorry for the accident victim.

examples.ko: 동정하지만 제가 도울 수 있는 일은 없어요.
examples.en: I feel for them, but there's nothing I can do to help.
Rather than pitying them, help together.

examples.ko: 그 이야기를 들으면 누구나 그를 동정할 거예요.
examples.en: Anyone who hears that story will feel sorry for him.

examples.ko: 동정하는 눈빛으로 보면 상대가 기분이 나빠요.
examples.en: If you look at someone with pity, they feel bad.

explain: 남의 어려움을 보고 불쌍하게 느낄 때 써요. '공감하다'는 같은 마음이 되는 것이고 '동정하다'는 위에서 내려다보는 느낌이 있어서 때로는 기분 나쁘게 들려요. 영어 sympathize보다 불쌍히 여긴다는 뜻이 강해요.
explain_en: Use it when you see someone's hardship and feel pity. '공감하다' is sharing the same feeling, while '동정하다' can feel like looking down from above and sometimes sounds unpleasant. It leans more toward pity than the English word sympathize.

examples.en: The principal presented awards to the winning students.
At the film festival, they present an award to this year's best actor.
They'll present awards from first to third place.

examples.ko: 시상하는 순서가 되자 모두 박수를 쳤어요.
examples.en: When it was time to present the awards, everyone clapped.
After the awards were presented, we took photos together.
Who will present the award this time?

explain: 상을 주는 일을 가리켜요. 보통 '시상식', '시상자'로 많이 쓰고, 동사는 '상을 주다'가 더 일상적이에요. '수상하다'는 상을 받는 쪽이라서 방향이 반대예요.
explain_en: It refers to giving out an award. Nouns like '시상식' (ceremony) and '시상자' (presenter) are more common, and in daily speech the verb phrase is '상을 주다'. '수상하다' is for the one who receives the prize, so the direction is opposite.
